title: Exact restriction and small free-sheaf presentations of its partial left adjoint
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in a common module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1). Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$, put $R'=R\circ u$, and let $T:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ be restriction $N\mapsto N\circ u$, with the induced $R'$-action [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $T$ is additive and exact. For either $(\mathcal E,S)=(\mathcal C,R')$ or $(\mathcal D,R)$ and each $U\in\mathcal E$, define $E_U^S=(S[h_U])^\#$, where $S[h_U](V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}S(V)$ and restriction sends $e_a$ to $e_{a\circ b}$ along $b:V'\to V$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The evaluation map $\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_U^S,M)\to M(U)$ sending $f$ to the image of $e_{1_U}$ is a bijection, natural in $M$. For every $S$-module sheaf $M$, the map $\bigoplus_{(U,s),\ s\in M(U)}E_U^S\to M$ whose $(U,s)$-component corresponds to $s$ is an epimorphism. All its indexing sets are small in the fixed universe. The class $\mathcal P$ of objects isomorphic to small sums of the $E_U^{R'}$ contains $0$, is closed under finite sums, and epimorphically generates $\operatorname{Mod}(R')$. For every small family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal C$ there are bijections, natural in $N\in\operatorname{Mod}(R)$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}\!\left(\bigoplus_i E_{U_i}^{R'},TN\right)\cong\prod_iN(uU_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R}\!\left(\bigoplus_i E_{uU_i}^{R},N\right),$$
whose components are these evaluation bijections.

source.place: Tag 0797, lemma-lower-shriek-modules, evaluation computation and reduction to partial adjoints; Tag 03EW, lemma-module-quotient-flat (3) and its proof. Exactness by the local-lifting argument for cocontinuity.

proof.text: Continuity makes $R'=R\circ u$ and the underlying abelian presheaf $N\circ u$ sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf]. The sectionwise action and restrictions obey $(ax)|_V=a|_Vx|_V$, so they define $TN$ and its maps by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For morphisms $f,g$, $(T(f+g))_U=f_{uU}+g_{uU}$, hence $T$ is additive. Kernels are sectionwise by the same definition node, and $(\ker f)(uU)=\ker(f_{uU})$ with the same restrictions and action. Thus $T(\ker f)=\ker(Tf)$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-ringed-restriction] to $u,R$, forgetting commutativity. Both sites are small in the stipulated common universe, and both continuity and cocontinuity are hypotheses. Its identity structural map makes its module restriction precisely $T$, and it supplies $T\dashv H$ for a module functor $H$. Cokernels exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. If $q:B\to Q$ is the cokernel of $f:A\to B$, adjunction identifies maps $TQ\to Z$ with maps $Q\to HZ$, hence with maps $b:B\to HZ$ satisfying $bf=0$. Naturality identifies these with maps $c:TB\to Z$ satisfying $c(Tf)=0$, and identifies precomposition by $Tq$ with precomposition by $q$. Thus $Tq$ has the cokernel universal property. Together with step 1 this proves exactness.

proof.text: For either ringed site $(\mathcal E,S)$, put $P_U(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}S(V)$. For $s\in M(U)$ define $\phi_{s,V}(\sum_a r_ae_a)=\sum_a r_aM(a)(s)$. Semilinearity of restrictions shows this is a morphism of module presheaves: along $b:V'\to V$ both composites give $\sum_a r_a|_{V'}M(ab)(s)$. Conversely, naturality and linearity force every $\phi:P_U\to M$ to have this formula with $s=\phi_U(e_{1_U})$, since $e_a$ is the restriction of $e_{1_U}$ along $a$. This is the presheaf bijection $\phi\mapsto\phi_U(e_{1_U})$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], applied to $M$ regarded as a presheaf of $S$-modules, with the inverse formula and naturality stated there. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\phi_s$ extends uniquely to $E_U^S=P_U^\#\to M$. These constructions are inverse. Here the image of $e_{1_U}$ in $E_U^S(U)$ means its image under the sheafification unit. For $h:M\to N$, linearity and naturality give $h_V\phi_{s,V}=\phi_{h_U(s),V}$, and unique extension gives naturality of the evaluation bijection.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 0797, lemma-lower-shriek-modules, displayed evaluation computation

proof.text: For $\mathcal G=S_U$ on $\mathcal E/U$, the formula in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] is exactly $P_U$: the summand for $a:V\to U$ is $S(V)$, and restriction along $b$ sends $r_ae_a$ to $r_a|_{V'}e_{ab}$. The statement of [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat] identifies $j_{U!}S_U$ with the sheafification of precisely this presheaf; thus it is the specified $E_U^S$ (only this identification, not flatness, is used). Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-quotient-j-shriek] to $\mathcal E,S,M$; its hypotheses are precisely smallness of $\mathcal E$ and commutativity of $S$. Its $(U,s)$ component $\psi_s$ is the map attached to $s$; by step 3, $\psi_s=\phi_{\theta(s)}$ for $\theta(s)\in M(U)$ its evaluation, and $s\mapsto\theta(s)$ is a bijection of $M(U)$, being the composite of two bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_U^S,M)\cong M(U)$. (For the standard adjunction $\theta$ is the identity, since the adjoint of $1\mapsto s$ sends the identity generator to $s$, but this is not needed.) Hence the required map $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}E_U^S\to M$ with components $\phi_s$ is the canonical epimorphism precomposed with the isomorphism of sums reindexing each $M(U)$ by $\theta$, so it is an epimorphism, for both $(\mathcal C,R')$ and $(\mathcal D,R)$.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero; Tag 03EW, lemma-module-quotient-flat (3) and its proof

proof.text: All coproducts in question exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. In the fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention], the objects of either site form a small set and each $M(U)$ is small. Consequently $\coprod_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal E)}M(U)$ is a small indexing set; all $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(V,U)$ and the stipulated sets $I$ are small as well. The empty sum is $0$. The sum of two sums indexed by $I,J$ is the sum indexed by $I\amalg J$: maps from either object are exactly pairs of families of component maps. Iteration proves closure under finite sums, also after replacing objects by isomorphic ones. Step 4 provides an epimorphism from such a small sum onto every $R'$-module sheaf, proving epimorphic generation by $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; Tag 03EW, lemma-module-quotient-flat (3), indexing by (U,s)

proof.text: Use the coproducts supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. A morphism from $\bigoplus_i E_{U_i}^{R'}$ is uniquely its family of composites with the inclusions. Step 3 identifies those composites with sections in $(TN)(U_i)=N(uU_i)$. In the other site step 3 identifies the same sections with maps $E_{uU_i}^{R}\to N$; the coproduct universal property assembles them uniquely to a map $\bigoplus_i E_{uU_i}^{R}\to N$. Reversing these operations is the inverse bijection. For $h:N\to N'$, both routes act on the $i$th section by $h_{uU_i}$, by step 3, proving naturality and the claimed component normalization. When $I$ is empty both Hom sets and the empty product have exactly one element.
